issues.explanation: Unique-race conversion is hand-rolled against SQLSTATE 23000 and messages containing 'UNIQUE'/'Duplicate'; PostgreSQL reports unique violations as 23505 with a lowercase 'duplicate key' message, so a race there would still surface as a raw QueryException instead of ValidationException.

The is_string branch json_decodes any string, so a corrupted value that is a JSON string containing a JSON array (double-encoded) becomes an array and grants access, although the spec says a corrupted non-array value must deny; the test only covers a JSON string scalar.

No test exercises the QueryException/race branch of CreateQueue or UpdateQueue, and no test has a granted employee calling through CallNextTicket, leaving the explicit race edge case and the second call path's positive case unverified.
The identical isUniqueViolation helper is copy-pasted into both actions; Laravel's UniqueConstraintViolationException or a shared helper would remove the duplication.

Entity::factory()->create() inside definition() persists a new entity even for make() and ignores an explicitly overridden queue, so the shared entity should be supplied via a state or closure instead.

review.summary: This change implements the queue lifecycle, per-queue access grants, the QueuePolicy, and authorization in both call paths, with the migration/model/factory, updated docs and a broad test suite. It is close to complete; the remaining concerns are DB-specific unique-race handling and a corrupted-permissions edge in QueuePolicy, plus minor test, duplication and factory nits.
